column1: # tools/contracts-modules-baseline.tsv — @depends/load-order disagreements that
# EXIST and are knowingly recorded by `tools/check-contracts.sh modules`.
# Shape: kind<TAB>key<TAB>why-it-is-recorded.  The key is the violating declaration,
# so fixing one edge makes exactly one row stale (the tool prints it as STALE and asks
# for the row's removal).  A key that is NOT here and appears in the tree FAILS.
# Why a baseline rather than a clean tree (measured 2026-09-23, the pass that added
# the check): the console's @depends headers declare RUNTIME collaborators as if they
# were load-order edges.  Two shapes:
#   * 09a/09c/09e (the OpenClaw group) declare the §11 LLM modules they call at run
#     time (so → model/serve/llm_*), but §9 loads before §11.
#   * 11a-11f are one mutually-recursive cluster: registry ↔ autotune ↔ model ↔
#     runtime, so each pair is a two-node cycle.
# Hard-failing on these would have landed a red gate and blocked every other change;
# recording them keeps NEW drift fatal (the point of the check) while the declarations
# are repaired.  Fixing them is a DECLARATION repair in the module headers, which is
# NOT this tool's change to make: 11b/11c/11d/11e are reserved by a concurrent
# session, and moving a runtime collaborator out of @depends needs an agreed field for
# it (the headers already use @state-in/@state-out for a related purpose).
# The strongest single signal that the declarations are the thing that is wrong:
# docs/inspection.md §9.4.1 states "Every module's @depends lists only modules with a
# lower numeric prefix. No circular dependencies." — 2026-09-23, that claim is false
# for 12 edges and 1 strongly-connected component.
# DELETE THIS FILE to make every row below fail: the recorded population is not
# enforcement, it is a debt list.
